size_pct_nav_at_cost: Large, approximately US$3.2bn initial purchase commitment reported March 2015 against approximately US$18bn January firm AUM; ratio approximately 18% is contextual, not an authenticated trade-date NAV weight. Later peak and added exposure excluded.

drivers.driver: Viewed existing assets as bought at a modest discount, but compounding through future acquisitions as the major source of additional intrinsic value.
Trusted Pearson and the acquisition/operating playbook after working together during the Allergan campaign.
Expected efficient cost structure, low tax burden and disciplined capital allocation to compound cash earnings.
drivers.source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/885590/000119312515059044/d879266dex991.htm (2015-02-23 management plan, not an Ackman quotation); https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2022/10/07154952/2016-Annual-Report-Letter-Only.pdf (Ackman retrospective)

drivers.driver: Mistake: highly acquisitive complexity made the result unusually dependent on managerial execution and judgment.
drivers.quote: The highly acquisitive nature of Valeant’s business required flawless capital allocation and operational execution, and therefore, a larger than normal degree of reliance on management. In retrospect, we misjudged the prior management team and this contributed to our loss.

entry_valuation_stated: Retrospective says modest discount to existing assets and larger discount assuming continued successful high-return acquisitions. This is not a quantified safety margin. At cutoff US$197.48 is 23.7x original FY2014 Cash EPS and 19.0–19.6x January 2015 pre-Salix guidance; actual trading began earlier.
outcome_note: Sold March 2017, widely reported approximately US$4bn aggregate loss; exact fund-level realized loss calculation not reconstructed here. Ackman's March 28 letter: 'Clearly, our investment in Valeant was a huge mistake.' Lessons include over-reliance on historical management performance, political/reimbursement exposure, sensitivity to assumptions, overpaying for Salix and permanent business/reputation damage after a price collapse. A good prior record was not an asset that guaranteed a stream of future high-return deals. Unlike the GGP legal/asset-coverage thesis, substantial Valeant value depended on future management action and a fragile pricing/acquisition model. Later investigations, Philidor and restatements are excluded from documents.
pack_quality_notes: Eight dated documents, original February 25 2015 10-K, earnings release, call, hostile-target critique, three-peer comparison and dated portfolio context. Cash EPS/CFO/reinvestment distinctions explicit; analyst consensus on Q4 reported, forward multiples use labeled pre-Salix management guidance. Historical rolling prices retrieved under successor symbol with cutoff bounded. Gaps: exact trade-date NAV weight, complete seven-position dollar table, consensus forward valuation and consistently acquisition-inclusive ROIC. The archival letter's bullet-page extraction is garbled, so entry-driver quotations are null/paraphrase rather than invented verbatim.
